THE RESPONSIVE CONTRACT, written in docs/design-system.md and enforced by scripts/layout-rules.test.ts and e2e/desktop.ts.

Widths:
- phone below 640 px (the mobile-first default), tablet 640–1023 px, desktop from 1024 px
- written only as (width >= 40rem), (width >= 64rem), their (width < …) forms, and (40rem <= width < 64rem)
- in rem, so a larger default text size moves to the narrower layout (WCAG reflow)
- written out in full, because custom properties cannot be used inside @media
- components adapt with container queries

Layout changes only in CSS:
- SSR paints the final layout, nothing shifts, and no route gains JS
- matchMedia is allowed only for reduced motion, colour scheme and display mode
- nothing reads the viewport size or listens for resize in order to lay out

Pointer and density:
- hover styles appear only under (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine), and hover is never the only cue
- targets stay at least 44 px and the type scale is the same at every width
- density comes from columns, because a 1024–1366 px screen can be a touch iPad

A screen declares its width with data-layout on its root element:
- readable is the default, for forms, text, settings such as Security, and conversations. It is --content-readable (40rem) from 640 px; the phone column stays --content-max (34rem).
- wide is --content-wide (72rem), for dashboards and grids
- split puts --content-list (20rem) beside the readable detail, for a list and its editor
- the rules live in the global stylesheet and read the attribute with :has(); a declaration costs about 12 B of initial JS

Fixed and sticky chrome comes in two kinds:
- Screen chrome belongs to a whole readable screen (Coach's composer) or to the app (toasts).
  - It is fixed at bottom: var(--nav-inset-bottom); toasts keep their top inset.
  - It is centred with left: calc(50% + var(--nav-inset-left) / 2) and is at most var(--content-column) wide.
  - Only readable screens have it at the bottom.
- Column chrome belongs to one column of a wide or split screen: an editor's Save bar, the Build preview's 'Start week 1', a session's actions.
  - From 1024 px it is position: sticky; bottom: var(--nav-inset-bottom), as the last child of its column, with no left offset and no transform. It therefore takes the column's width and never covers another column.
  - No ancestor up to the column may set overflow.
  - Below 1024 px the column is the whole content, so it may stay fixed screen chrome.
- Neither kind is ever offset by --nav-height. Outside the shell the insets are 0.
- Specs check chrome against the element it belongs to: expectInColumn(chrome, owner) or expectCentredOver(chrome, main) for screen chrome. A screen that later turns from readable to split therefore keeps its older specs green.

THE EMAIL LINK LANDS ON THE SIGN-IN SCREEN.
- The emailed URL is <relying-party origin>/?link#t=<token>. There is no new route, because a route node costs every screen 30 B or more.
- The token sits in the URL fragment, which browsers never send:
  - it never reaches a server, a Vercel log or a Referer header
  - a scanner that fetches the URL gets the sign-in page without the token, so prefetching is harmless by design
  - the verify endpoint has no GET handler
- On load, the page removes the token from the address bar. It posts the token only when the owner taps Sign in.
- ?link lets the server render finish mode without a flash.
- Redirects drop the fragment explicitly. A Location without a fragment inherits the request's (RFC 9110 §10.2.2), so every redirect the load makes for /?link carries an empty one:
  - an owner session goes to <next>#
  - a recovery session goes to /recover/passkey#
  - a recovery session never redeems a link: it goes on to add a passkey, and the link stays unused for its 15 minutes (open question)
- Finish mode uses AuthScreen, so it gets the desktop layout too.
- The link is built from the relying party's origin, never from the request's Host header. In production that is exactly https://coach.nikocruz.com.

THE SAME ANSWER, ALWAYS: RESPOND FIRST.
- The request endpoint reads no body. It answers 202 {ok: true} with no-store before doing any work.
- Everything that depends on state runs after the response, through waitUntil: the per-client and global limits, the owner and setup check, issuing the link, sending the mail and the audit.
- Status, body, headers, timing and Server-Timing are therefore identical in every case: a link sent, a limit hit, no owner, or a provider failure. No response floor is needed, and hooks.server.ts does not change.
- Refused requests write only the existing first-refusal audit row, so a flood of requests is not a flood of rows.
- The inbox notice is worded for this: 'nothing after a few minutes? try again later or use your passkey'.
- With the feature off, both endpoints answer 404. That reveals configuration, not account state.

TOKEN AND LIFECYCLE.
- The token is 32 bytes from randomBytes: the existing generateToken, 256 bits, 43 base64url characters.
- Only its SHA-256 is stored, in email_sign_in_links. The owner FK cascades, so withCommitted's truncate clears the table.
- CHECKs cap the lifetime at 15 minutes and keep used and revoked mutually exclusive.
- Redeeming a link is one conditional UPDATE … WHERE the link is unused, unrevoked and unexpired and setup is complete … RETURNING. It runs inside the transaction that rotates the presented session and issues the new one, so two concurrent redemptions cannot both match.
- A new link revokes the owner's older live links under the owner row lock, so concurrent requests leave one live link.
- 'Sign out everywhere else' revokes pending links, and auth:reset-owner deletes them.
- Nothing is sent or redeemed while setup is open.
- Links are pruned a day after they expire.

NO BROWSER BINDING (Plan B's binding cookie is not adopted; open question).
- A link bound to the browser that asked fails in realistic owner flows:
  - a desktop mail client opens the default browser, not the one that asked
  - Gmail on iPhone opens links in its own in-app browser
  - the owner asks on the laptop and opens the mail on the phone
- Binding protects little:
  - an attacker who has the mailbox can press the button in their own browser and receive a link bound to it
  - so binding stops only leaks of a link the owner asked for (forwarding, a pasted URL)
  - single use, the 15-minute expiry, newest-only and the step-up wall already limit those
- ASVS 2.7.3 is recorded as Partial for this reason. 2.7.4 is a Deviation, because email is not a secure independent channel (NIST SP 800-63B §5.1.3.1 does not accept it as an out-of-band authenticator), with the same compensating controls.
- If the owner wants binding, it is one cookie and one column, added to email-link-schema and email-link-service before they merge.

SESSION.
- A link gives a full session:
  - kind owner, method email_link
  - the same 30-day idle and 90-day absolute lifetime as a passkey session (open question)
  - reauthenticated_at null
- The existing requireRecentAuthentication then refuses these actions until a passkey step-up: adding or removing passkeys, new recovery codes, and signing devices out. reauth.ts does not change; integration and e2e tests prove it.
- The presented session is rotated, whatever its kind. A direct POST that presents a recovery session gets it revoked and replaced, which grants nothing the token does not already grant in a fresh browser. The page itself never offers finish mode to a signed-in visitor.
- Security labels the session 'with email link'. The label is server-side, so it costs no client JS.
- The activity feed pins 'Signed in with an email link' as a significant event, so floods never push it out.
- There is no extra badge or Profile line, because each would cost initial JS on the tightest routes.

LIMITS (policy.ts).
- Requests:
  - email.request: 5 per 15 minutes per client (an IPv4 address or an IPv6 /64)
  - email.hourly: 10 per hour across all clients
  - email.daily: 20 per day across all clients
  - at most about 620 mails a month, inside Resend's free tier of 100 a day and 3,000 a month
- Verification: email.verify, 10 per 15 minutes per client. Tokens are unguessable, so this only limits noise.
- The bucket names fit security.md's 17-character Bucket column. The audit events keep the email_link.* names.
- Verification answers 429 like every other auth endpoint. The person holding a token already knows that it exists, so the 'same answer' rule does not apply there.
- RATE_LIMIT_PRUNE.staleAfterMs rises to 2 days, so it stays longer than every window.
- A flood can use up the daily cap and switch email sign-in off until the next day. Passkeys are unaffected (open question).

ONLY THE OWNER'S ADDRESS; PROVIDER; CONFIGURATION.
- The recipient:
  - OWNER_EMAIL comes from the environment only
  - a mailer is created with its recipient, and send() has no recipient parameter, so no caller can address mail anywhere else
  - tests assert that every recorded message goes to the configured address, also when the request body carries another address
  - the address never appears in the repository (the no-personal-address guard), in a page, or in a page's data
- The mail layer:
  - a leaf layer with its own ESLint block
  - calls Resend's API with fetch, with no SDK and no new dependency
  - sends plain text only
  - uses the link id as Idempotency-Key, a 10 s timeout and one attempt
  - errors carry the status and Resend's error name, never the key or the text (the text holds the token)
- The test adapter:
  - chosen whenever test routes are enabled and allowed, even with a key present, so a test server never sends real mail
  - impossible on Vercel or in a Vercel build
- Preview deployments are always off.
- The three variables never stop the server. Missing or invalid values switch the feature off, and the startup log names them.
- The feature stays off in production until the owner follows docs/deployment.md's switch-on steps, which land with the complete security reference in docs-email-security.
- The e2e server and the Lighthouse server both get a test OWNER_EMAIL with test routes on: the option is shown, and any request goes to the recording mailer, never to Resend.

slices.goal:

requestSignInLink(request, ctx) is the work a request triggers after its answer has been sent, so nothing in it can change what the requester sees.

- It sends nothing when a limit is hit, when no owner has completed setup, or when the origin is not the app's own.
- Otherwise it stores a new link: a 256-bit CSPRNG token, SHA-256 only, valid 15 minutes, with older live links revoked.
- It mails the plain-text message through a mailer bound to OWNER_EMAIL, and audits each outcome.
- It never throws.

completeEmailSignIn(token, presentedToken, request):
- consumes the link atomically and rotates the presented session, whatever its kind
- issues a full owner session with method email_link and no step-up freshness, so adding or removing passkeys, new recovery codes and signing devices out still ask for a passkey

openQuestions:
Browser binding. A link works in any browser for its 15 minutes, once, and only the newest link is valid. Binding each link to the browser that asked (Plan B's design: one cookie and one column) would refuse forwarded links. It would also refuse the owner's own link in common cases:
- opened from a desktop mail client in another browser
- opened from Gmail's in-app browser
- opened on the phone after asking on the laptop

Keep links unbound?

Migration timing. The email link's database half waits for M3's last schema slot (db-explain, m3/33), as the brief says, so the feature ships near the end of M3's backend work. The alternative is to take the slot right after coaching-memory-db (m3/24), and have db-explain regenerate any index migration on top. Keep the brief's order?
Link-session lifetime. A link session lives as long as a passkey session (30 days idle, 90 days absolute). Should it be shorter, say 14 days absolute, because email is the weaker factor?

Superseding. A new request voids earlier unused links, and anyone can press the button. A stranger can therefore void a link the owner has not opened yet; the owner receives both emails and uses the newest. Is that acceptable?

Limits.
- Requests: 5 per 15 minutes per client, 10 per hour and 20 per day overall.
- Verifications: 10 per 15 minutes per client.
- A flood can use up the daily cap and switch email sign-in off until the next day; passkeys are unaffected.

Accept these values?
Expiry. The owner chose 15 minutes; ASVS 2.7.2 says 10. Keep 15 minutes, recorded as a deviation?

Recovery session and links. A link opened in a browser that holds a recovery session (after a recovery code) is ignored: the session goes on to add a passkey, and the link stays usable for its 15 minutes. Should it instead upgrade the session to a full one?

Installed iPhone app. The link opens in Safari or the mail app's own browser, which do not share cookies with the installed app, so it signs in that browser. The option stays visible in the installed app, with one line saying so. Should it be hidden there instead?

Keyboard order. The nav moves before <main> (at most 8 B on app routes), so on desktop the Tab order matches the rail on the left. On iPhone, VoiceOver then reads the tab bar before the content, though nothing moves visually. Accept this, or keep the old order and reach the rail after the content on desktop?
Rail or sidebar. From 1024 px the plan uses an 88 px rail with labels under the icons. Is a wider sidebar, with labels beside the icons, wanted from 1280 px? It is a CSS-only change.

Brand mark colour. The rail's mark draws its arc in --color-accent, the same volt as the favicon in both themes. On the white light-theme rail the volt arc is pale; --color-accent-text would read darker. Keep the volt?
Tablet. From 640 to 1023 px the bottom bar stays and the column widens from 34 to 40 rem; iPad landscape (1024 px and up) gets the rail. Confirm?

Security on desktop. Security keeps the readable column at 1440 px, as a settings screen (0 B). Two columns (passkeys and devices beside codes and activity) would cost 12 B of initial JS with a data-layout attribute, or 0 B as a CSS-only :has() declaration in Security's own stylesheet. Wanted?

Security's dates. Formatting Security's dates on the server as well would save 261 B more on the tightest route. The dates would then follow the profile's time zone instead of the device's zone as today, and the profile's zone stays UTC until onboarding or M3's Build records the device's. Keep them in the browser unless M2's or M3's route nodes need the bytes?

Train on desktop. The plan keeps M3's selected-day rendering and lays it out in two columns under a full-width week strip. A seven-day grid with every session visible would change M3's rendering and cost initial JS on /train. Is it wanted later, in M8?
Desktop Lighthouse in CI. It is measured locally and recorded in the docs. Asserting it in CI adds about 5 minutes per run. Is that wanted?
Security notices. With a mailer in place, security follow-up 3 becomes cheap: an email when a passkey is added, a recovery code is used or the owner is reset. Plan it as a PR after M2X?
